This coverage is already duplicated safely elsewhere: resolve_dir([]) == "handoffs" is already a pure unit test at line 419 (F-DIR-DEFAULT), and the banner-threading integration (run/1 actually prints "under <dir>" for whatever resolve_dir returns) is already proven end-to-end at line 521 (T-DIR-SCOPED-SCAN) using a tmp fixture via --dir -- same code path, no real-corpus dependency. Fixing this test drops zero net coverage.

result.summary:
Independently re-read test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs (lines 380-699) before designing -- confirmed all three tests ISSUE-FIXER named exist exactly as claimed: F-DIR-DEFAULT (lines 416-420) is a pure unit assertion `LintHandoffs.resolve_dir([]) == "handoffs"`, no directory scan, no capture_io; T-DIR-SCOPED-SCAN (lines 521-533) exercises run/1's full banner-printing path end-to-end against an isolated System.tmp_dir!/0 fixture via --dir, asserting `io =~ inspect(dir)` (same banner format T-DEFAULT-NO-FLAG-SCANS-REAL-CORPUS checks for, just against a safe fixture instead of the real corpus); T-DEFAULT-NO-FLAG-SCANS-REAL-CORPUS (lines 686-698) is confirmed to do exactly what ISSUE-FIXER described -- capture_io around LintHandoffs.run([]) == :ok, plus io =~ under \"handoffs\". Also independently confirmed resolve_dir/1 (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex:354-360) is public, takes no filesystem action itself (pure case over find_dir_flag/1's return), and is unchanged by this fix.

Design written to lib/letflow/design/iss0523-lint-handoffs-corpus-coupling-fix.md. Chose option (i): rewrite the test body in place to `assert LintHandoffs.resolve_dir([]) == "handoffs"` with an explanatory comment, keeping the test's name/slot. Justified against this file's own precedent: the test's existing docstring (lines 687-693) already narrates its own narrowed scope in place rather than being deleted once narrowed, and the file's convention throughout (ISS-0440/ISS-0442 section banners, the mutant-table note, the empty-dir carve-out note) is to keep a name-addressable test slot with an inline comment stating current scope, not to delete slots and point elsewhere -- keeping the searchable test name matters for future grep/`--only` use and for incident-report traceability the way ISS-0445 itself needed. Option (ii) was weighed and rejected as needing two edits (both F-DIR-DEFAULT and T-DIR-SCOPED-SCAN) to replace what one docstring currently conveys as a single coherent claim.

Crux question (design section 3) answered explicitly: removing the real-corpus assertion leaves NO net coverage gap. Confirmed by direct reading (not assumed) that mix.exs line 105 lists \"letflow.lint_handoffs\" inside the letflow.check alias chain, and .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 50-55 carry a comment stating mix letflow.lint_handoffs is one of letflow.check's own CI steps (and is why the workflow uses fetch-depth: 0). So the real mix task, scanning the real corpus, already runs as its own CI gate step independent of mix test -- and a real violation surfaces there with correct attribution (a corpus-hygiene gate failing), not smuggled into an unrelated branch's test-suite result the way the ISS-0445 incident's misattribution happened.

Test-ability (design section 4): no fail-then-pass proof needed for the rewritten assertion -- it's byte-identical to F-DIR-DEFAULT's already-passing claim, no application-code change occurred. TEST-DESIGNER should instead positively verify the OLD coupling is gone: a one-time manual/review-time check (not a new permanent test, to avoid reintroducing corpus-touching risk) of temporarily writing a violation-tripping scratch file into handoffs/, confirming the rewritten test still passes, then removing it; plus a full-suite regression run of the test file confirming green regardless of the corpus's current state.
